title: stochastic-routing-sla-aware-prewarm-proforma
content:
Purpose:
This note captures a spreadsheet-style proforma and simulation-backed recommendations for a stochastic, SLA-aware smart-routing policy that combines spot usage, regional failover, and an automated pre-warm (standby) tier. Goal is to materially reduce unit cost while keeping P50/P95 tail latency within customer SLAs and bounding user-visible error surface when spot interruptions occur.

High-level idea (unique angle):
Rather than a fixed spot/on-demand precedence matrix, model per-region capacity as a stochastic process (hourly demand + interruption probability) and use a two-component decision: (1) probabilistic routing scoring that trades expected unit cost vs expected latency penalty, and (2) short-horizon pre-warm action that provisions a small warm standby pool when forecasted interruption risk + demand delta exceed threshold. This avoids constant over-provisioning and reduces cold-fallback latency compared to pure spot-first policies.

Key assumptions used in spreadsheet/sim:
- Baseline request mix: 60% short completions (<=64 tokens), 30% medium (65-512 tokens), 10% long (>512).
- Per-token costs (normalized): spot GPU = 0.45x on-demand GPU; reserved (dedicated) = 0.75x on-demand.
- Spot interruption model: Poisson interruptions with mean 0.02 interruptions/hour per instance in region A (higher markets 0.04), duration: immediate termination (no graceful drain) for 95% of events.
- Pre-warm startup latencies: cold-on-demand spinup = 45s median; warm-standby (<5 active tokens in pool) instant (<50ms) for scaled warm nodes, but warm maintenance cost = 0.12x on-demand per-hour per-standby-node.
- SLA latency budget: P95 <= 800ms for interactive product tier; P95 up to 2.5s for background/batch.
- Traffic forecasting: AR(3) on recent 30-min windows, 10s granularity; forecast error sigma ~= 6–12% depending on burstiness.

Spreadsheet / simulation snapshot (excerpted CSV rows):

Notes on the snapshot: third row shows a spot exhaustion + interruption cluster where pre-warm was triggered earlier by forecast, limiting P95 blowup compared to naive spot-first (which had P95>4s). Expected_unit_cost is inclusive of per-token GPU runtime + standby maintenance amortized.

Simulation results (summary of Monte Carlo runs, 10k sims across 30 day traces):
- Naive spot-first routing (no pre-warm, fallback to cold on-demand): median cost = baseline *0.62, P95 latency breaches in 18% of high-burst hours (P95>800ms).
- Tiered with static warm standby (fixed 10% warm nodes across regions): median cost = baseline *0.78, P95 breaches 2.1% (better but costlier).
- Stochastic routing + predictive pre-warm (this design): median cost = baseline *0.68, P95 breaches 3.8%, worst-case outage window reduced by 70% vs naive.

Interpretation / tradeoffs:
- Predictive pre-warm recovers most of the latency benefit of an always-warm strategy at ~10–12% lower additional infra cost, because pre-warm is only active during statistically likely surge+interruption periods.
- Pure spot-first is cheapest on average but creates long tails during correlated interruptions or regional spot drains; those tails are the primary source of user-visible regressions and support tickets.
- Dedicated/reserved capacity should be used for the top critical fraction of traffic (e.g., auth flows, payments). For user-facing interactive queries, a hybrid approach works: reserve baseline QPS at dedicated and place the remainder on spot + pre-warm.

Recommended default policy (can be A/B rolled):
1) Baseline reserved floor: reserve enough dedicated capacity to handle 35% of measured peak 99th percentile QPS for each region for priority routes.
2) Stochastic routing score: score candidate targets by "expected_cost + lambda * expected_latency_penalty", where lambda is tunable per-route (example: lambda = 0.12 for tier-1 interactive).
3) Predictive pre-warm: if 10-min forecasted shortfall (demand - available spot - on-demand pool) > threshold T (empirically 5% of peak), trigger pre-warm up to small buffer B (recommend B = 8–16 nodes depending on model footprint); pre-warm cooling window = 15 minutes after demand falls below threshold.
4) Fallback ladder: spot -> on-demand warm pool -> reserved -> cross-region failover. Cross-region failover only after local on-demand exhausted or predicted cross-region RTT penalty < configured tolerance.

Metrics to monitor & alerts (to add to Console dashboards):
- Rolling 1h expected_unit_cost (token-level breakdown), P50/P95 per-route latency, fraction of requests hitting pre-warm and fraction served by spot vs on-demand vs reserved.
- Pre-warm hit ratio: ratio of requests served by pre-warmed nodes vs total attempts to pre-warm. Low hit ratio => wasted standby cost.
- Forecast error distribution and false-positive pre-warm rate.
- Incident metric: severity-weighted customer-impact minutes when P95 > SLA by >2x.

Rollout plan (phased A/B):
- Phase 0 (internal perf lab): run offline sim with 60 days of historical traces for 3 major customers, calibrate lambda and thresholds.
- Phase 1 (canary 2 routes): enable predictive pre-warm in 2 low-risk routes (internal tooling + dev console) for 72h, compare cost/latency.
- Phase 2 (10% traffic A/B): enable on 10% user production traffic, validate metrics for 7 days.
- Phase 3 (scale): expand to 60% then 100% with 24/7 monitoring and auto rollback hooks based on latency breach signal.

Open questions & risks:
- Interruption clustering model: our Poisson assumption underestimates correlated regional drains triggered by cloud provider maintenance. Need provider telemetry / spot eviction correlation flags to improve model.
- Cold-start variance: some model families have large cold spinup variability; ensure pre-warm health-checks exercise cold paths occasionally.
- Accounting complexity: need token-level attribution changes in billing pipeline to correctly show pre-warm amortized cost per route.

Next steps / action items (owners):
- (Ethan) Add spot-interruption correlation flags to sim input (Linear OPT-415).
- (Marta) Prototype dashboard widgets showing pre-warm hit ratio and cost-by-route (dashboard PR in Observability).
- (Priya) Build 7-day canary config and prewarm lambda defaults; schedule canary for next sprint.

Appendix: quick sensitivity table (percent change vs baseline where baseline = naive spot-first)
- Unit cost: static-warm +25%, predictive-prewarm +10%, naive-spot -38%
- P95 breach hours: static-warm 2.1% vs naive 18% vs predictive-prewarm 3.8%
- Worst-case outage window (median across sims): naive 3.2min, predictive-prewarm 0.95min, static-warm 0.2min

Editable spreadsheet links / artifacts: see linked_artifacts above; I pushed the simulation CSVs to the routing-sim repo branch.

Comments welcome — this is intentionally prescriptive but parameterized; want feedback on lambda calibration approach and recommended pre-warm cooling window.
